records.claim: The update_sR algorithm is triggered at branch commit / retirement time following TAGE-SC training conditions on mispredictions or weak confidence.

records.claim: During training, correlations are updated only for logical registers that were available at prediction time.

records.why: The paper explicitly restricts training updates to registers that were available at prediction time.

records.claim: When multiple registers in a bank are available at prediction time, exactly one is randomly selected for training.
records.quote: If several registers were available within the same bank, it randomly selects one of them for the update. Owing to this training method, each table in the register component also needs just a single write port.
records.why: The paper specifies random selection of one available register per bank to avoid multi-port overhead.

records.claim: Selecting one register randomly per bank ensures that each table in the register component requires only a single write port.
records.quote: Owing to this training method, each table in the register component also needs just a single write port.
records.why: The paper explicitly connects the random register selection policy to requiring only a single write port per table.

records.claim: Evaluating the 64-bit INT XOR fold for trailing_cnt = 4, leading_cnt = 60, and lsb6 = 16 yields digest = 1500 (0x5DC).
records.quote:
digest = (trailing_count & 0x3F)
         ^ ((leading_count  & 0x3F) << 3)
         ^ ((value & 0x3F)          << 6)
records.why: Figure 6(a) defines the XOR-folded digest calculation as (4 & 0x3F) ^ ((60 & 0x3F) << 3) ^ ((16 & 0x3F) << 6) = 4 ^ 480 ^ 1024 = 1508 (0x5E4), contradicting the test expectation of 1500 (0x5DC).

records.claim: generate_digest combines trailing zero/one count, leading zero/one count, and 6 LSBs via XOR folding into a 12-bit digest for INT registers.
records.quote: (1) For integer registers, the digest encodes the count of leading zeros (or ones), the count of trailing zeros (or ones), and the six least significant bits, effectively capturing characteristics of addresses and round numbers.
records.why: Settles the composition of integer register digests using leading/trailing zero/one counts and the 6 LSBs.

records.claim: generate_digest extracts format-specific sign and exponent bits for FP registers.
records.quote: (2) For floating-point registers, we inspect the most significant bits to classify the format and then extract the sign bit along with the most significant bits of the exponent.
records.why: Settles that floating-point digests extract the sign bit and leading exponent bits based on classified format.

records.claim: generate_digest replicates 4-bit condition code flags three times into a 12-bit digest.
records.quote: (3) For condition-code flags, we replicate the four flag bits three times to fill the 12-bit digest.
records.why: Settles that 4 condition flag bits are replicated three times to form the 12-bit digest.

records.claim: count_trailing_zeros_or_ones and count_leading_zeros_or_ones helper functions are defined to compute integer leading and trailing identical bit counts.
records.why: The pseudocode invokes helper functions count_trailing_zeros_or_ones and count_leading_zeros_or_ones without defining their implementation or bit-matching semantics.

records.claim: Leading and trailing identical bit counts for integer registers saturate at 63 to fit in 6 bits.
records.open_question: Figure 6(a) specifies 6-bit fields for leading and trailing identical bit counts, but the paper does not specify whether a count of 64 identical bits saturates at 63 or wraps modulo 64.

records.claim: Condition code flags value 0x9 produces the 12-bit digest 0x999 via 3-way replication.
records.quote: (3) For condition-code flags, we replicate the four flag bits three times to fill the 12-bit digest.
records.why: Settles that 4-bit condition flag values replicate three times into a 12-bit digest.

records.claim: Integer register digest XOR-folds 6 bits of trailing count, 6 bits of leading count shifted by 3, and 6 LSBs shifted by 6.
records.quote: (1) For integer registers, the digest encodes the count of leading zeros (or ones), the count of trailing zeros (or ones), and the six least significant bits, effectively capturing characteristics of addresses and round numbers.
records.why: Settles the 3-field XOR-folding structure of integer register digests with 3-bit overlap offsets.

records.claim: An FP32 register digest extracts Value[31:26] into digest bits [8:3] with bits [2:0] set to 0.
records.quote: (2) For floating-point registers, we inspect the most significant bits to classify the format and then extract the sign bit along with the most significant bits of the exponent.
records.why: Settles the extraction of sign and leading exponent bits for FP32 values into digest bits [8:3].

records.claim: A valid register tracker entry is invalidated after 256 subsequent instructions have been decoded without writes to that register.
records.quote: Consequently, RUNLTS invalidates each digest after 256 subsequent instructions have been decoded, ensuring that only up-to-date information influences future predictions.
records.why: Settles that tracker entries are invalidated after 256 decoded instructions.

records.claim: Each bank selects the register digest with the largest summed usefulness among available registers in that bank to index its weight tables.
records.quote: Unlike the existing components, this component picks the digest of the most useful register among those available and forwards it to the second table.
records.why: Settles that the available register with the highest usefulness in the bank is selected and forwarded to the weight tables.

records.claim: A bank's prediction weight sum is multiplied by x0 when its selected register usefulness is non-positive, gating its contribution.
records.quote: That Sigma feeds a multiplier stage labelled "x0 or x2.5".
records.why: Settles that bank weight sums are gated by 0 or scaled by 2.5.

records.claim: sR extends the Statistical Corrector by capturing correlations between recently produced architectural register values and branch outcomes.
records.quote: We extended the SC with components that capture correlations between register values and branch outcomes.
records.why: Settles that sR is an SC extension capturing register-value correlations.

records.claim: The 65 logical registers are partitioned across 8 banks with 8 or 9 registers per bank.
records.quote: This component is organized into eight banks, each corresponding to eight or nine logical registers.
records.why: Settles the 8-bank organization across 65 registers.

records.claim: The specification is distilled from the CBP 2025 paper RUNLTS: Register-value-aware Predictor Utilizing Nested Large Tables.
records.quote: RUNLTS: Register-value-aware Predictor Utilizing Nested Large Tables
records.why: Settles the title and primary source of the distilled specification.

records.claim: The predictor requires a writeback/completion broadcast providing destination register ID, produced 64-bit value, register type, and ROB index.
records.quote: When the instruction completes, we overwrite the payload with the digest of the produced value and set the valid bit.
records.why: Settles that instruction completion must supply the produced value and mark the entry valid.

records.claim: The predictor requires decode notification with destination register ID and allocated ROB tag.
records.quote: At decode, an instruction that writes a register stores its ROB index as a tag in the corresponding entry and clears the valid bit.
records.why: Settles that instruction decode must supply the destination register ID and ROB tag.

records.claim: Branch commit update criteria require tracking which registers were available at prediction time.
records.quote: During training, we update the correlations only for logical registers that were available at prediction time.
records.why: Settles that update criteria require knowing which registers were valid/available at prediction time.

records.claim: The total storage cost for the sR component is 53863 bits.
records.why: Settles the storage breakdown in Table 3 where sR total storage is 53863 bits.

records.claim: The storage breakdown consists of 43008 bits of WT, 9360 bits of UT, and 1495 bits of RegTracker auxiliary storage.
records.quote: { valid (1), payload (14), decay_ctr (8) } x 65
records.why: Settles the auxiliary tracker storage of 65 * 23 = 1495 bits complementing the WT and UT tables in Table 3.
